title.narrative: TRUE-FISH (EU-EAC True Fish Farming Story in Lake Victoria Basin)

description.narrative: The project will seek to remove some key impediments (access to commercial networks and availability of skilled workers) and key risks (spreading of diseases and loss of biodiversity) to the long-term sustainability of aquaculture in the Lake Victoria Basin.The projects aims to contribute to develop competitive, gender equitable and sustainable commercial aquaculture (governance and productive activities) with 3 main objectives: business, skills and sustainability. Activities are implemented by FAO, Landell Mills and Worldfish and coordinated by Lake Victoria Fisheries Organisation (LVFO).

title.narrative: Increased number of formal employment in aquaculture in LV Basin (disaggregated by gender)

description.narrative: Formal employment refers to those employees formally working at commercial aquaculture farms, that have been certified by official institutions, and specifically by the participating TVETs.

comment.narrative: The sectorial Training Need Assessment conducted by TRUEFISH in 2020 found that out of the 15 of formal employees who have aquaculture training only 16 have received formal aquaculture degrees after completion of their training. That means that less than 2 of the total workers in 2020 has a formal certificate.

The intervention foresees an increase of at least 18 in the formal employment of employees holding a formal degree issued by the participating TVETs. This value is assuming that private operators are ready and willing for absorbing these graduates within the lifespan of the project.
